title: Oklahoma 44, Baylor 34: First Visitor to Win at McLane
question: When did Oklahoma beat Baylor 44-34 at McLane Stadium in 2015?
answer: On November 14, 2015, No. 12 Oklahoma beat No. 6 Baylor 44-34 in Waco. The Sooners ended Baylor's 20-game home winning streak and became the first visiting team to win at McLane Stadium.
summary: On Nov. 14, 2015, No. 12 Oklahoma won 44-34 at No. 6 Baylor, ending a 20-game home streak and becoming the first visitor to win at McLane Stadium.
body: On this date in 2015, Oklahoma traveled to Waco for one of the biggest Big 12 games of the season. The Sooners were ranked No. 12 and Baylor was No. 6, playing at McLane Stadium, a building that had not yet seen a visiting team leave with a win.

That changed on a rainy Saturday night. Oklahoma won 44-34, ending Baylor's 20-game home winning streak, the longest in the FBS at the time, and became the first visitor to win at McLane since the stadium opened.

Baker Mayfield completed 24 of 34 passes for 270 yards and three touchdowns, and he added 76 rushing yards. Samaje Perine ran 28 times for 166 yards, including a 55-yard touchdown in the third quarter that stretched the lead to 34-20. Sterling Shepard caught 14 passes for 177 yards.

Oklahoma led 20-13 at halftime, and Baylor's freshman quarterback Jarrett Stidham kept the Bears close with 257 passing yards. Mayfield sealed it with a seven-yard touchdown pass with 4:47 left, making it 44-34.
The win pushed Oklahoma to 9-1 and badly hurt Baylor's College Football Playoff hopes. It also kept the Sooners on the path to a Big 12 title and their first playoff berth.
